title: For Your Consideration: Animated and Documentary Short Films by Op-Docs
text:
Supported by
Op-Docs
For Your Consideration: The New York Times Op-Docs Short Films
Living With a Visionary
A husband learns to navigate life while caring for his wife of 50 years as she experiences vivid hallucinations.
La Retaguardia (The Ones Who Stay)
Four artists in Havana grapple with whether to remain in Cuba amid a profound national crisis.
Listen
As his mother slips away into dementia, an Alaskan sound recordist listens for what remains.
Sanyi Kakas (Sanyi the Rooster)
In 2020, a rooster escaped from the poultry market in Bekescsaba, Hungary. For four years, the locals cared for him as a beloved symbol of hope and unity — until his sudden, mysterious death replaces harmony with suspicion and division.
SON
A mother begins communicating with her son through the graffiti tags he leaves around the city.
Stalin Boys
Four Texas middle school students develop an unusual fascination with Joseph Stalin while preparing a history fair project.
The Tuners
In the shadows of the International Chopin Piano Competition, one of the world’s most important classical music contests, expert tuners spend weeks trying to achieve the perfect pitch.
COMING SOON
A Wolf in the Suburbs
Welcome to Mississauga, Ontario, where lawns are clipped, neighbors are watchful and no blade of grass dares misbehave. Except at Wolf Ruck’s place. His lawn grows wild, and so does the trouble.
COMING SOON
The Revolution Against Death
A faded rococo resort hosts a revolution against aging and death. Amid turquoise pools, gilt and chintz, fear is in the air — of illness, of invisibility, of having no one to hold or hear us, of dying alone. A film poem about mortality, fear, the longing to remain when you know you can’t.
COMING SOON
